bottom_line: China restricts export of gallium, germanium, and rare earth processing technology, creating structural supply risk for semiconductor and defense supply chains.
what_changed: China Ministry of Commerce announced export licensing requirements for gallium, germanium, antimony, and related processing technology.
why_it_matters: China controls 60-90% of global processing for these minerals; licensing creates discretionary supply disruption tool.
main_uncertainty: Licensing may be selectively enforced; alternative supply development timelines are 3-7 years.

scenarios.name: Selective restriction
scenarios.description: Licenses granted to allied countries, denied to others.
indicators: Differentiated approval rates by destination country
diplomatic linkage to other trade disputes

scenarios.name: Broad restriction
scenarios.description: Export volumes drop across all destinations.

watch_next: Export license approval rates published by MOFCOM
